facts.fact: Home affairs minister Leon Schreiber demonstrated the department's digital ID on his phone in the MyMzansi app on 1 October 2026, and TechCentral reports an operational digital ID is targeted for 2027/2028.

ZAF.note: Home affairs is described as holding the civil registry and identity records, but no link between them is stated.
No digital civil registration system is stated.
MyMzansi is described only as a digital ID demonstration; no online government service is stated as available.
No enrolment count or share is stated.
No number at birth is stated.
The document says only that core infrastructure will be built in Sars's hosting environment; operation and maintenance are not stated.
No public register keyed on the ID number is stated.

facts.fact: TechCentral reports that home affairs and Sars signed a digital pact in April 2025, the digital ID's core infrastructure will be built in Sars's hosting environment, and Treasury has set aside R150-million for the MyMzansi app, with an operational digital ID targeted for 2027/2028.

ZAF.note: No digital entry at local registration offices is stated.
